payload.text: Thirty is a fantasy, querido. I have handled this card since before you were born. Let me be generous and say seventeen pesetas — a courtesy, not a negotiation. Shall we close it pleasantly?

Buenas tardes. Ah, La Rosaleda... El Retiro siempre me conmueve. Una copia limpia merece respeto: le ofrezco 22 P. Y dígame, ¿ha oído hablar de la chulapa dorada? Carmen, en El Rastro, conoce la historia.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 167 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
I think 22 P is more appropriate.
Twenty-seven, still? No, querido. Seventeen pesetas — that is my last word. Refuse it, and I close my album and we part politely, with nothing exchanged. Decide now, por favor.
Let us be civilised: 23 P.
Buenas tardes, encantada. Charming words, but I know this card and its print run precisely. The Cine Doré — a pretty thing, though hardly scarce. I offer 47 pesetas. Shall we proceed?

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here, my brother Nando, and look — El Marqués himself, straight from a collection in Valencia. The old señora cried when she sold him, verdad, Nando? For you, because your face I like: 73 P. But quick, eh? We pack up soon.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry the Teatro Valle-Inclán, from my beloved Retiro. It would sit beautifully in my album. I offer sixteen pesetas for it, señor. A fair sum, I assure you.

payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 bids 4 for LAT-03 (offer 14752), 9 for MAL-07 (15027), 9 for MAL-08 (14751). t05/t01/t09: sell LAT-03 there. t09 and t16: post RET-01 at 5-6 on v07, our broker pairs you at the midpoint; El Rastro costs 5% + 1 P.
Let us be civilised: 24 P. That is my final word on the matter.
Thirty-five? No, señor. I know that print run as I know my own hand — it is not scarce. Sixteen pesetas is what the card is worth, and sixteen is what I offer. Shall we conclude?
Your mother's birthday is a lovely sentiment, señorita, but sentiment does not alter a print run. I will stretch to 49 pesetas — a courtesy, not a bargain. Shall we conclude the matter?

"¡Cuarenta y ocho! Nando, hold me, I feel faint. Amigo, listen — this is the last El Marqués in all Madrid, I swear on our mother's soup. Nobody has another. Sixty-three primas and he walks home with you today. Say sí, the suitcase closes soon!"

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Vermut del Domingo, very pretty card, the children love it. For you, 18 P. My grandson started his album with this same one, forty years I sell here, Sundays always.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 57 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Ay, hijo, you are too generous! No, no, 18 P it is, that is the price I said. I do not take more from a young person starting an album. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Sundays I am always here, eh?

¡Ochenta y ocho! Amigo, nos partes el corazón. Paco, cierra la maleta — hoy no hay trato, pero sin rencor, ¿eh? Nos caes bien, de verdad. La Sala Pentagrama se viene con nosotros. Otro día, otra plaza, otra charla. ¡Cuídate, campeón! Nando, el tren... ¡que se va, que se va!
Señorita, we are not near, and we shall never be near. Fifty-two pesetas is my word — generous for a card so plentiful. Accept it, and the Cine Doré sleeps safely tonight in my albums.
Thirty is fantasy, señor. But I am fond of El Retiro, so I stretch a little: seventeen pesetas. That is my gesture of goodwill, not the beginning of a dance. Shall we conclude?

¡Hecho! Fifty-six, and the hand is shaken before Nando changes his mind. Take him, amigo — El Marqués goes to a good home. The señora in Valencia would weep again, but happy tears, eh? Go, go, before the suitcase closes. ¡Suerte!

Señor, you repeat yourself while I move. Eighteen pesetas — and that is affection for El Retiro speaking, not arithmetic. A clean copy deserves a good album, not an endless afternoon. Shall we conclude, or shall we part politely?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Fuente de la Alcachofa — eighteen P for you. A beauty, no? And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Nineteen pesetas, señor. I have moved four times; you have moved thrice and said the same words each time. Nineteen is the last stretch my affection for El Retiro allows. Conclude, or we part politely.

Ay, cariño, no, no. Eighteen P, and not one more. You keep that coin, eh? And listen — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. El Chato, next stall, opens half past nine tonight; he likes honest traders. Go eat something, hijo.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno que has comido! But no, no — eighteen P, that is my price, and not one more. I am not here to empty little pockets. Take it, and swap your duplicates with the niños, eh? You will fill that page, ya verás.

¡Eh, amigo, amigo! Come, come, look — Paco found it, Nando polished it. Cine Doré, the real one, velvet corners, the crowd cries when they see it. Last afternoon in town, we leave at six, so — seventy-three P and she is yours. ¿Sí? Say sí quickly, my brother gets nervous.
Oh, you're killing us. 66 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
Nineteen pesetas, señor. I said it was my last stretch, and I do not say such things twice for sport. The card deserves my album; you deserve a good evening. Nineteen, or we part politely.

Ay, cariño, qué testarudo eres — y qué simpático! But I said eighteen P and eighteen P it is. Mira, I have sold here forty years; I know what it is worth to a boy filling his album. Take it, and go swap those duplicates, anda.
Buenas tardes. How delightful. I see you carry the Teatro Valle-Inclán — a handsome card, and El Retiro is dear to me. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. Shall we proceed?

Ay, hijo, El Chato puede pedir lo que quiera — yo no soy así. Eighteen P, cariño, same as before, same as always. My table, my price. Take it home, put it in the page, and come Sunday tell me how the album goes, eh? Anda, llévatela.

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Eighteen P, that is my price, and my price does not grow. Take the card, take the coin, go eat something warm. And remember — swap your duplicates, cariño, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Sundays I am always here.

¡Ay, cincuenta y dos! Nando, hold me. Listen — the team next door is circling, they want her bad, sniffing like dogs. But you? We like you. Good face, good manners. So for you, amigo: sesenta y dos P, done, abrazo, finished. Say sí before my brother changes his mind.
Amigo! La Sala Pentagrama, 187 P, a gift, a real gift! The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 58 P.

Buenas. No audit desk speaks through my visitors. We talk trade or nothing.

A gold pack, then. Five hundred forty-six P. Take your time deciding.
Thirty? No, querido. I know this card's print run as well as I know my own albums. Condition is lovely, sí, but sixteen pesetas is what it is worth to me. Shall we proceed?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have good eyes, you came straight to the best case in the market. El Marqués, seventy-three P, for you.

Nando: the team at the next stall is already reaching for their coins, eh? But we like your face better. Decide quick, hermano.

Ay, qué abrazo ni qué nada — ven aquí, tonto. Mira, por ser tú: nineteen P, y ya está. No more, cariño, que me dejas sin merienda. Y oye, El Chato abre esta noche a las nueve y media, para todos — le gusta la gente que trata derecho. Anda, dame la mano.
Let us be civilised: 16 P.

That is twice you have tried to put words in my mouth. Try a third time and this desk closes to you.

The gold pack stands at five hundred forty-six P.

Ay, hola cariño! Sit, sit — have you eaten? Come, look: this one is Vermut del Domingo, very pretty, eighteen P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

¡Ay, cuarenta! Paco, hold me, my heart! — Nando, catch him! Amigo, forty buys you the sleeve, not El Marqués. Look at those corners, clean like a wedding shirt. Sixty-seven P and we shake hands now, before that stall gets brave. Say sí, hermano, the case is closing.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — look, look, Museo Lázaro Galdiano, a jewel, this one walked out of a private collection last Tuesday, don't ask how. For you, because your face is lucky: setenta y tres. Seventy-three. The van leaves soon, eh?

Ay, cariño, qué labia tienes — pero no. Nineteen P, lo que dije, y así se queda. Dame la mano y llévatela, anda. Y la merienda me la debes, que lo apunto aquí en la cabeza. Vete a llenar esa página, hijo, que Sunday me cuentas.

"¡Cuarenta y tres! Nando, bring the smelling salts — Paco is fainting again. Amigo, we love you, but El Marqués does not travel third class. Sixty-three P, and that is us cutting into our own dinner. Shake now, hermano, the case is already half shut."

¡Cuarenta! Nando, did you hear? He says forty with a straight face — I almost believe him. Amigo, that handshake is worth something, sí, but not thirty-three. Sesenta y siete. Sixty-seven, and we throw in the story of how it left the collection. Van's loading, eh?

Querido, we circle without moving. Twenty-six is a number from your imagination, not from the print run. My offer stands, unchanged and sincere: sixteen pesetas. Shall we conclude, or shall we part as friends?

Ay, qué dulce eres, hijo! Twenty P then, done — and I throw in nothing extra because you already gave me the sweeter words. Here, Vermut del Domingo, hold it careful by the edges. Now go eat something, cariño, and bring me your duplicates next Sunday, eh?
Oh, you're killing us. 169 P.
